# Disaster Relief Goods Inventory and Distribution Management System

An AI-driven, priority-focused inventory management and distribution system aligned with **UN Sustainable Development Goal 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities)**.

---

## 📖 Background of the Study

### Target Organizations & Key Stakeholders
* **Global & Primary Partner:** Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) / UN-Habitat / UN-Habitat Philippines
* **Government Partners:** Department of Transportation (DOTr), Office of Civil Defense (OCD), National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA)
* **Community Alliances:** Union of Local Authorities of the Philippines (ULAP), United Nations Youth Association of the Philippines (UNYAP)

> **Core Function:** These entities coordinate urban risk reduction, policy implementation, community-level disaster response, and local relief operations across Philippine barangays.

### Overview of the Existing System
The current disaster response pipeline relies on a **hybrid, paper-based operational process**:
1. **Reporting:** Disaster needs are relayed manually from barangays to Local Government Units (LGUs) via paper logs, SMS, or radio.
2. **Inventory Tracking:** Physical counts are recorded manually in paper logbooks and basic spreadsheets at central storage hubs.
3. **Allocation:** Relief supplies are packaged into standardized bundles regardless of specific community urgency or special needs.
4. **Logistics:** Delivery routes and dispatch schedules are assigned manually by logistics officers.

### Operational Bottlenecks & Impact
| Bottleneck | Operational Impact |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⏱️ **Time-Consuming Procedures** | Physical counts and manual data entry create severe dispatch bottlenecks during critical disaster windows. |
| ❌ **Information Loss & Errors** | Paper logs cause frequent tracking errors, duplicate distribution lists, and missing inventory records. |
| 🚚 **Delayed Dispatch & Zero Visibility** | Lack of real-time tracking creates communication breakdowns between LGU staff, donors, and affected communities. |
| ⚠️ **Lack of Priority Allocation** | Critical goods (medicine, clean water) are bundled and shipped alongside low-priority items without urgency sorting. |
| 🚨 **Public Safety Risks & Waste** | Staff waste vital hours cross-checking logs, resulting in delayed aid, expired perishables, and misallocated supplies. |

### Need for Modernization
The disaster relief pipeline requires an automated, modern system to replace paper log processing and dynamically route goods based on real-time community urgency.

#### References & SDGs
* [UN SDGs Goal 11: Teams & Partners](https://philippines.un.org/en/sdgs/11/teams-partners)
* [DOST STI4SDG: Sustainable Cities and Communities](https://sti4sdg.dost.gov.ph/index.php/2024/09/01/11sustainablecitiesandcommunities/)
* [UN Pacific SDGs Goal 11](https://pacific.un.org/en/sdgs/11)
* [Local Government Academy (LGA) Publication](https://cdn.lga.gov.ph/publication/attachments/1590478478.pdf)

---

## 🎯 Project Objectives

1. **Inventory Management System:** Centralize stock tracking for LGU and barangay officials to record, monitor, update, and manage relief goods in real time.
2. **Disaster & Beneficiary Management System:** Track disaster incidents, affected families, individuals, and their specific assistance requirements.
3. **Donation Management System:** Automatically record incoming relief contributions and update available inventory dynamically.
4. **Distribution Management System:** Log the release of goods to beneficiaries and automatically deduct distributed items from inventory.

---

## 📦 Expected Output

The primary output is a web-based **Disaster Relief Goods Management System** featuring:
* **Accessible & Intuitive UI:** Tailored for LGU and Barangay Officials, incorporating accessibility features for Persons with Disabilities (PWD) personnel.
* **Core OOP Inventory Computation:** Deterministic algorithms leveraging Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts for exact inventory tracking.
* **AI-Assisted Reasoning Module:** An integrated AI model that analyzes community urgency levels, prioritizes essential goods, and assists in optimized dispatch decisions.

---

## 💡 Significance of the Study

This study advances software engineering and management research by demonstrating how **Artificial Intelligence can be layered onto classic Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) architectures**. Rather than completely replacing existing operational frameworks, this hybrid model tests how AI can enhance decision-making, priority sorting, and resource allocation without adding prohibitive costs or operational complexity.

---

## 👥 Target Beneficiaries

| Stakeholder Group | Expected Value & Outcome |
| :--- | :--- |
| **LGU & Barangay Staff** | Eliminates manual logbooks, reduces paperwork errors, and speeds up dispatch workflows. |
| **Barangay Residents** | Receives urgent, life-saving supplies faster and tailored to immediate community needs. |
| **Donors & NGOs** | Gains full transparency into inventory levels, ensuring aid reaches intended communities without waste. |
| **UN Organizations & DILG** | Obtains reliable data logging supporting SDG 11 urban risk reduction frameworks. |
| **PWD Personnel** | Interacts with an inclusive, accessible system interface designed for diverse operational roles. |
| **Future Researchers** | Serves as a baseline study for combining traditional software architectures with AI-driven logistics. |

# Disaster Relief Goods Inventory and Distribution Management System

An AI-driven, priority-focused inventory management and distribution system aligned with **UN Sustainable Development Goal 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities)**.

---

## 📖 Background of the Study

### Target Organizations & Key Stakeholders
* **Global & Primary Partner:** Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) / UN-Habitat / UN-Habitat Philippines
* **Government Partners:** Department of Transportation (DOTr), Office of Civil Defense (OCD), National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA)
* **Community Alliances:** Union of Local Authorities of the Philippines (ULAP), United Nations Youth Association of the Philippines (UNYAP)

> **Core Function:** These entities coordinate urban risk reduction, policy implementation, community-level disaster response, and local relief operations across Philippine barangays.

### Overview of the Existing System
The current disaster response pipeline relies on a **hybrid, paper-based operational process**:
1. **Reporting:** Disaster needs are relayed manually from barangays to Local Government Units (LGUs) via paper logs, SMS, or radio.
2. **Inventory Tracking:** Physical counts are recorded manually in paper logbooks and basic spreadsheets at central storage hubs.
3. **Allocation:** Relief supplies are packaged into standardized bundles regardless of specific community urgency or special needs.
4. **Logistics:** Delivery routes and dispatch schedules are assigned manually by logistics officers.

### Operational Bottlenecks & Impact
| Bottleneck | Operational Impact |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⏱️ **Time-Consuming Procedures** | Physical counts and manual data entry create severe dispatch bottlenecks during critical disaster windows. |
| ❌ **Information Loss & Errors** | Paper logs cause frequent tracking errors, duplicate distribution lists, and missing inventory records. |
| 🚚 **Delayed Dispatch & Zero Visibility** | Lack of real-time tracking creates communication breakdowns between LGU staff, donors, and affected communities. |
| ⚠️ **Lack of Priority Allocation** | Critical goods (medicine, clean water) are bundled and shipped alongside low-priority items without urgency sorting. |
| 🚨 **Public Safety Risks & Waste** | Staff waste vital hours cross-checking logs, resulting in delayed aid, expired perishables, and misallocated supplies. |

### Need for Modernization
The disaster relief pipeline requires an automated, modern system to replace paper log processing and dynamically route goods based on real-time community urgency.

#### References & SDGs
* [UN SDGs Goal 11: Teams & Partners](https://philippines.un.org/en/sdgs/11/teams-partners)
* [DOST STI4SDG: Sustainable Cities and Communities](https://sti4sdg.dost.gov.ph/index.php/2024/09/01/11sustainablecitiesandcommunities/)
* [UN Pacific SDGs Goal 11](https://pacific.un.org/en/sdgs/11)
* [Local Government Academy (LGA) Publication](https://cdn.lga.gov.ph/publication/attachments/1590478478.pdf)

---

## 🎯 Project Objectives

1. **Inventory Management System:** Centralize stock tracking for LGU and barangay officials to record, monitor, update, and manage relief goods in real time.
2. **Disaster & Beneficiary Management System:** Track disaster incidents, affected families, individuals, and their specific assistance requirements.
3. **Donation Management System:** Automatically record incoming relief contributions and update available inventory dynamically.
4. **Distribution Management System:** Log the release of goods to beneficiaries and automatically deduct distributed items from inventory.

---

## 📦 Expected Output

The primary output is a web-based **Disaster Relief Goods Management System** featuring:
* **Accessible & Intuitive UI:** Tailored for LGU and Barangay Officials, incorporating accessibility features for Persons with Disabilities (PWD) personnel.
* **Core OOP Inventory Computation:** Deterministic algorithms leveraging Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts for exact inventory tracking.
* **AI-Assisted Reasoning Module:** An integrated AI model that analyzes community urgency levels, prioritizes essential goods, and assists in optimized dispatch decisions.

---

## 💡 Significance of the Study

This study advances software engineering and management research by demonstrating how **Artificial Intelligence can be layered onto classic Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) architectures**. Rather than completely replacing existing operational frameworks, this hybrid model tests how AI can enhance decision-making, priority sorting, and resource allocation without adding prohibitive costs or operational complexity.

---

## 👥 Target Beneficiaries

| Stakeholder Group | Expected Value & Outcome |
| :--- | :--- |
| **LGU & Barangay Staff** | Eliminates manual logbooks, reduces paperwork errors, and speeds up dispatch workflows. |
| **Barangay Residents** | Receives urgent, life-saving supplies faster and tailored to immediate community needs. |
| **Donors & NGOs** | Gains full transparency into inventory levels, ensuring aid reaches intended communities without waste. |
| **UN Organizations & DILG** | Obtains reliable data logging supporting SDG 11 urban risk reduction frameworks. |
| **PWD Personnel** | Interacts with an inclusive, accessible system interface designed for diverse operational roles. |
| **Future Researchers** | Serves as a baseline study for combining traditional software architectures with AI-driven logistics. |

For these classes, **you probably don’t need inheritance yet**. Most relationships in this system are “has a” relationships, called **association** or **composition**—one object refers to another.

### The relationships that fit your system

- A **Beneficiary is associated with a Disaster**: the person or household is affected by that disaster. A beneficiary is **not** a kind of disaster.
- A **Donation is associated with Inventory**: the donation contributes a particular item to stock.
- A **Distribution is associated with a Beneficiary and Inventory**: it records who received which item.
- An **Audit record is associated with a UserAccount** and the action being recorded.
- A **Report uses information from** disasters, beneficiaries, inventory, donations, and distributions.

That matches the references in [Beneficiaries.java](C:/Users/danie/OneDrive/Documents/GitHub/Disaster-Relief-Goods-Inventory-and-Distribution-Management-System/Beneficiaries.java), [Donations.java](C:/Users/danie/OneDrive/Documents/GitHub/Disaster-Relief-Goods-Inventory-and-Distribution-Management-System/Donations.java), [Distribution.java](C:/Users/danie/OneDrive/Documents/GitHub/Disaster-Relief-Goods-Inventory-and-Distribution-Management-System/Distribution.java), and [Audits.java](C:/Users/danie/OneDrive/Documents/GitHub/Disaster-Relief-Goods-Inventory-and-Distribution-Management-System/Audits.java).

### Where inheritance might fit

The UI/UX activity has three account roles: Admin, Barangay Official, and Encoder. You **could** make `Admin`, `BarangayOfficial`, and `Encoder` subclasses of `UserAccount` if they need different behavior. But if they mostly share the same account data and only differ by role, the `Role` enum in [UserAccount.java](C:/Users/danie/OneDrive/Documents/GitHub/Disaster-Relief-Goods-Inventory-and-Distribution-Management-System/UserAccount.java) is simpler and sufficient.

### One important distinction

Your current fields hold **one reference** to another object. For example, a `Distribution` refers to one beneficiary and one inventory object. In the real system, one disaster may have many beneficiaries, and one beneficiary may have many distributions. You can represent those many-record relationships later using a database or collections; you don’t need inheritance for them.

**Bottom line:** keep the current classes separate and connect them with references. Add inheritance only if you later find genuinely different kinds of objects that share data but need different behavior.

* **Government Partners:** Department of Transportation (DOTr), Office of Civil Defense (OCD), National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA)
* **Community Alliances:** Union of Local Authorities of the Philippines (ULAP), United Nations Youth Association of the Philippines (UNYAP)

> **Core Function:** These entities coordinate urban risk reduction, policy implementation, community-level disaster response, and local relief operations across Philippine barangays.

### Overview of the Existing System
The current disaster response pipeline relies on a **hybrid, paper-based operational process**:
1. **Reporting:** Disaster needs are relayed manually from barangays to Local Government Units (LGUs) via paper logs, SMS, or radio.
2. **Inventory Tracking:** Physical counts are recorded manually in paper logbooks and basic spreadsheets at central storage hubs.
3. **Allocation:** Relief supplies are packaged into standardized bundles regardless of specific community urgency or special needs.
4. **Logistics:** Delivery routes and dispatch schedules are assigned manually by logistics officers.

### Operational Bottlenecks & Impact
| Bottleneck | Operational Impact |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⏱️ **Time-Consuming Procedures** | Physical counts and manual data entry create severe dispatch bottlenecks during critical disaster windows. |
| ❌ **Information Loss & Errors** | Paper logs cause frequent tracking errors, duplicate distribution lists, and missing inventory records. |
| 🚚 **Delayed Dispatch & Zero Visibility** | Lack of real-time tracking creates communication breakdowns between LGU staff, donors, and affected communities. |
| ⚠️ **Lack of Priority Allocation** | Critical goods (medicine, clean water) are bundled and shipped alongside low-priority items without urgency sorting. |
| 🚨 **Public Safety Risks & Waste** | Staff waste vital hours cross-checking logs, resulting in delayed aid, expired perishables, and misallocated supplies. |

### Need for Modernization
The disaster relief pipeline requires an automated, modern system to replace paper log processing and dynamically route goods based on real-time community urgency.

* [UN SDGs Goal 11: Teams & Partners](https://philippines.un.org/en/sdgs/11/teams-partners)
* [DOST STI4SDG: Sustainable Cities and Communities](https://sti4sdg.dost.gov.ph/index.php/2024/09/01/11sustainablecitiesandcommunities/)
* [UN Pacific SDGs Goal 11](https://pacific.un.org/en/sdgs/11)
* [Local Government Academy (LGA) Publication](https://cdn.lga.gov.ph/publication/attachments/1590478478.pdf)

1. **Inventory Management System:** Centralize stock tracking for LGU and barangay officials to record, monitor, update, and manage relief goods in real time.
2. **Disaster & Beneficiary Management System:** Track disaster incidents, affected families, individuals, and their specific assistance requirements.
3. **Donation Management System:** Automatically record incoming relief contributions and update available inventory dynamically.
4. **Distribution Management System:** Log the release of goods to beneficiaries and automatically deduct distributed items from inventory.

---

## 📦 Expected Output

The primary output is a web-based **Disaster Relief Goods Management System** featuring:
* **Accessible & Intuitive UI:** Tailored for LGU and Barangay Officials, incorporating accessibility features for Persons with Disabilities (PWD) personnel.
* **Core OOP Inventory Computation:** Deterministic algorithms leveraging Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts for exact inventory tracking.
* **AI-Assisted Reasoning Module:** An integrated AI model that analyzes community urgency levels, prioritizes essential goods, and assists in optimized dispatch decisions.

---

This study advances software engineering and management research by demonstrating how **Artificial Intelligence can be layered onto classic Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) architectures**. The role system in your UI proposal gives us a natural place to use them:

- **Abstraction:** make `UserAccount` an abstract base class.
- **Inheritance:** create `AdminAccount`, `BarangayOfficialAccount`, and `EncoderAccount` subclasses.
- **Polymorphism:** let each account type implement its own permissions. For example, an official can approve a distribution, while an encoder cannot; the controller can ask the account whether it has permission without checking its concrete class.
- **Encapsulation:** keep the account data private and expose appropriate methods.

That’s a better fit than forcing inheritance between things like `Donation` and `Inventory`, which aren’t “is-a” relationships. The next step should be to model the account roles this way, then use those permissions in the controllers.

# Disaster Relief Goods Inventory and Distribution Management System

An AI-driven, priority-focused inventory management and distribution system aligned with **UN Sustainable Development Goal 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities)**.

---

## 📖 Background of the Study

### Target Organizations & Key Stakeholders
* **Global & Primary Partner:** Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) / UN-Habitat / UN-Habitat Philippines
* **Government Partners:** Department of Transportation (DOTr), Office of Civil Defense (OCD), National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA)
* **Community Alliances:** Union of Local Authorities of the Philippines (ULAP), United Nations Youth Association of the Philippines (UNYAP)

> **Core Function:** These entities coordinate urban risk reduction, policy implementation, community-level disaster response, and local relief operations across Philippine barangays.

### Overview of the Existing System
The current disaster response pipeline relies on a **hybrid, paper-based operational process**:
1. **Reporting:** Disaster needs are relayed manually from barangays to Local Government Units (LGUs) via paper logs, SMS, or radio.
2. **Inventory Tracking:** Physical counts are recorded manually in paper logbooks and basic spreadsheets at central storage hubs.
3. **Allocation:** Relief supplies are packaged into standardized bundles regardless of specific community urgency or special needs.
4. **Logistics:** Delivery routes and dispatch schedules are assigned manually by logistics officers.

### Operational Bottlenecks & Impact
| Bottleneck | Operational Impact |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⏱️ **Time-Consuming Procedures** | Physical counts and manual data entry create severe dispatch bottlenecks during critical disaster windows. |
| ❌ **Information Loss & Errors** | Paper logs cause frequent tracking errors, duplicate distribution lists, and missing inventory records. |
| 🚚 **Delayed Dispatch & Zero Visibility** | Lack of real-time tracking creates communication breakdowns between LGU staff, donors, and affected communities. |
| ⚠️ **Lack of Priority Allocation** | Critical goods (medicine, clean water) are bundled and shipped alongside low-priority items without urgency sorting. |
| 🚨 **Public Safety Risks & Waste** | Staff waste vital hours cross-checking logs, resulting in delayed aid, expired perishables, and misallocated supplies. |

### Need for Modernization
The disaster relief pipeline requires an automated, modern system to replace paper log processing and dynamically route goods based on real-time community urgency.

#### References & SDGs
* [UN SDGs Goal 11: Teams & Partners](https://philippines.un.org/en/sdgs/11/teams-partners)
* [DOST STI4SDG: Sustainable Cities and Communities](https://sti4sdg.dost.gov.ph/index.php/2024/09/01/11sustainablecitiesandcommunities/)
* [UN Pacific SDGs Goal 11](https://pacific.un.org/en/sdgs/11)
* [Local Government Academy (LGA) Publication](https://cdn.lga.gov.ph/publication/attachments/1590478478.pdf)

---

2. **Disaster & Beneficiary Management System:** Track disaster incidents, affected families, individuals, and their specific assistance requirements.
3. **Donation Management System:** Automatically record incoming relief contributions and update available inventory dynamically.
4. **Distribution Management System:** Log the release of goods to beneficiaries and automatically deduct distributed items from inventory.

# Disaster Relief Goods Inventory and Distribution Management System

An AI-driven, priority-focused inventory management and distribution system aligned with **UN Sustainable Development Goal 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities)**.

---

## 📖 Background of the Study

### Target Organizations & Key Stakeholders
* **Global & Primary Partner:** Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) / UN-Habitat / UN-Habitat Philippines
* **Government Partners:** Department of Transportation (DOTr), Office of Civil Defense (OCD), National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA)
* **Community Alliances:** Union of Local Authorities of the Philippines (ULAP), United Nations Youth Association of the Philippines (UNYAP)

> **Core Function:** These entities coordinate urban risk reduction, policy implementation, community-level disaster response, and local relief operations across Philippine barangays.

### Overview of the Existing System
The current disaster response pipeline relies on a **hybrid, paper-based operational process**:
1. **Reporting:** Disaster needs are relayed manually from barangays to Local Government Units (LGUs) via paper logs, SMS, or radio.
2. **Inventory Tracking:** Physical counts are recorded manually in paper logbooks and basic spreadsheets at central storage hubs.
3. **Allocation:** Relief supplies are packaged into standardized bundles regardless of specific community urgency or special needs.
4. **Logistics:** Delivery routes and dispatch schedules are assigned manually by logistics officers.

### Operational Bottlenecks & Impact
| Bottleneck | Operational Impact |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⏱️ **Time-Consuming Procedures** | Physical counts and manual data entry create severe dispatch bottlenecks during critical disaster windows. |
| ❌ **Information Loss & Errors** | Paper logs cause frequent tracking errors, duplicate distribution lists, and missing inventory records. |
| 🚚 **Delayed Dispatch & Zero Visibility** | Lack of real-time tracking creates communication breakdowns between LGU staff, donors, and affected communities. |
| ⚠️ **Lack of Priority Allocation** | Critical goods (medicine, clean water) are bundled and shipped alongside low-priority items without urgency sorting. |
| 🚨 **Public Safety Risks & Waste** | Staff waste vital hours cross-checking logs, resulting in delayed aid, expired perishables, and misallocated supplies. |

### Need for Modernization
The disaster relief pipeline requires an automated, modern system to replace paper log processing and dynamically route goods based on real-time community urgency.

#### References & SDGs
* [UN SDGs Goal 11: Teams & Partners](https://philippines.un.org/en/sdgs/11/teams-partners)
* [DOST STI4SDG: Sustainable Cities and Communities](https://sti4sdg.dost.gov.ph/index.php/2024/09/01/11sustainablecitiesandcommunities/)
* [UN Pacific SDGs Goal 11](https://pacific.un.org/en/sdgs/11)
* [Local Government Academy (LGA) Publication](https://cdn.lga.gov.ph/publication/attachments/1590478478.pdf)

---

## 🎯 Project Objectives

1. **Inventory Management System:** Centralize stock tracking for LGU and barangay officials to record, monitor, update, and manage relief goods in real time.
2. **Disaster & Beneficiary Management System:** Track disaster incidents, affected families, individuals, and their specific assistance requirements.
3. **Donation Management System:** Automatically record incoming relief contributions and update available inventory dynamically.
4. **Distribution Management System:** Log the release of goods to beneficiaries and automatically deduct distributed items from inventory.

The controllers currently work with in-memory objects; database persistence and login authentication are not implemented yet.

---

## 📦 Expected Output

The primary output is a web-based **Disaster Relief Goods Management System** featuring:
* **Accessible & Intuitive UI:** Tailored for LGU and Barangay Officials, incorporating accessibility features for Persons with Disabilities (PWD) personnel.
* **Core OOP Inventory Computation:** Deterministic algorithms leveraging Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts for exact inventory tracking.
* **AI-Assisted Reasoning Module:** An integrated AI model that analyzes community urgency levels, prioritizes essential goods, and assists in optimized dispatch decisions.

1. **Inventory Management System:** Centralize stock tracking for LGU and barangay officials to record, monitor, update, and manage relief goods in real time.
2. **Disaster & Beneficiary Management System:** Track disaster incidents, affected families, individuals, and their specific assistance requirements.

---

## MVC Backend

The Java domain classes are the **Model** layer and own business rules such as transaction approval, role permission checks, and stock changes. `UserAccount` is an abstract base class; `AdminAccount`, `BarangayOfficialAccount`, and `EncoderAccount` inherit from it and override permission methods. Accounts hold a barangay workspace where applicable, an email, active/inactive status, and a salted PBKDF2 password hash. `LoginController` can authenticate against an in-memory account list; SQL-backed account lookup and persistence are still pending.

Feature controllers coordinate calls to the models, while the GUI/View can call the controller methods when it is added. Each `Barangay` is a workspace for its inventory, disasters, evacuation centers, households, and staff. `Beneficiaries` represents a household with individual `FamilyMember` records; household size and vulnerability counts derive from that roster, and a designated member represents the household head. Donation lines create distinct `InventoryBatch` records with received and optional expiry dates. Opening inventory is represented as an opening batch. Distribution lines can specify the batch to release; if only one batch has stock, it can be inferred, but the model requires an explicit batch when several are available rather than assuming an expiry/FIFO policy. Transaction and account data remain in memory until database persistence is added.

* **AI-Assisted Reasoning Module:** An integrated AI model that analyzes community urgency levels, prioritizes essential goods, and assists in optimized dispatch decisions.

## Important decisions for the GUI

- **Barangay workspaces:** Each official or encoder is assigned to a barangay. Users should work with records in their own workspace; admins can access all barangays.
- **Disaster access:** All active roles may create or update disaster records within a barangay they can access.
- **Households and members:** A household must have at least one confirmed member when registered. It keeps individual family-member records, with one designated head representing the household when receiving aid.
- **Homeless households:** For a homeless household, use the barangay’s name as the address.
- **Member details:** Age and senior/infant/PWD classifications are separate, independently entered values. The system should not infer a person’s category from their age; the person entering the data verifies the classification.
- **Inventory batches:** Each logged receipt is a separate batch, with its own quantity and optional expiry date. If multiple batches have available stock, the user must select which batch to distribute; the system does not assume FIFO or choose by expiry.
- **Transaction approvals:** Donations and distributions follow `DRAFT → PENDING → APPROVED` or `REJECTED`. Only approval changes inventory.
- **MVC and current scope:** The backend models hold data and business rules, controllers coordinate actions, and the GUI is a separate View. The Java classes are grouped in the `LIB` package; see the [README](</C:/Users/danie/OneDrive/Documents/GitHub/Disaster-Relief-Goods-Inventory-and-Distribution-Management-System/README.md>) for the project notes.

## Project phases

### Phase 1 — Structure
**Core structure is in place.** The `LIB` package contains the main models, controllers, role classes, and workspace relationships. The models include households and family members, evacuation centers, inventory batches, and transaction approval states. The code compiles, but some older controller creation methods still need to be avoided or tightened before the GUI relies on them.

### Phase 2 — SQL
**Not started.** The database still needs its schema, connection and persistence code, and integration with the models. Important design points include storing household/member relationships, barangay workspace assignments, donation and distribution item lines, batches, account password hashes and salts, and transaction status. Stock approval and transaction status updates should be atomic in the database. Report generation and automatic audit recording are also deferred until this phase.

### Phase 3 — GUI
**Not started.** Build the screens and connect them to the controllers. The GUI should reflect the decisions above—for example, show the active barangay workspace, require a confirmed member roster for household registration, provide an explicit homeless-household option, and require batch selection when more than one batch is available.

### Phase 4 — Final Testing and Debugging
**Not started.** Test the full flow from the GUI through SQL, including role and barangay access, household registration and aid release, batch-level stock changes, approval/rejection, and error handling. Also check reports and audit history once those features are implemented.

# Disaster Relief Goods Inventory and Distribution Management System

An AI-driven, priority-focused inventory management and distribution system aligned with **UN Sustainable Development Goal 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities)**.

---

## 📖 Background of the Study

### Target Organizations & Key Stakeholders
* **Global & Primary Partner:** Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) / UN-Habitat / UN-Habitat Philippines
* **Government Partners:** Department of Transportation (DOTr), Office of Civil Defense (OCD), National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA)
* **Community Alliances:** Union of Local Authorities of the Philippines (ULAP), United Nations Youth Association of the Philippines (UNYAP)

> **Core Function:** These entities coordinate urban risk reduction, policy implementation, community-level disaster response, and local relief operations across Philippine barangays.

### Overview of the Existing System
The current disaster response pipeline relies on a **hybrid, paper-based operational process**:
1. **Reporting:** Disaster needs are relayed manually from barangays to Local Government Units (LGUs) via paper logs, SMS, or radio.
2. **Inventory Tracking:** Physical counts are recorded manually in paper logbooks and basic spreadsheets at central storage hubs.
3. **Allocation:** Relief supplies are packaged into standardized bundles regardless of specific community urgency or special needs.
4. **Logistics:** Delivery routes and dispatch schedules are assigned manually by logistics officers.

### Operational Bottlenecks & Impact
| Bottleneck | Operational Impact |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⏱️ **Time-Consuming Procedures** | Physical counts and manual data entry create severe dispatch bottlenecks during critical disaster windows. |
| ❌ **Information Loss & Errors** | Paper logs cause frequent tracking errors, duplicate distribution lists, and missing inventory records. |
| 🚚 **Delayed Dispatch & Zero Visibility** | Lack of real-time tracking creates communication breakdowns between LGU staff, donors, and affected communities. |
| ⚠️ **Lack of Priority Allocation** | Critical goods (medicine, clean water) are bundled and shipped alongside low-priority items without urgency sorting. |
| 🚨 **Public Safety Risks & Waste** | Staff waste vital hours cross-checking logs, resulting in delayed aid, expired perishables, and misallocated supplies. |

### Need for Modernization
The disaster relief pipeline requires an automated, modern system to replace paper log processing and dynamically route goods based on real-time community urgency.

#### References & SDGs
* [UN SDGs Goal 11: Teams & Partners](https://philippines.un.org/en/sdgs/11/teams-partners)
* [DOST STI4SDG: Sustainable Cities and Communities](https://sti4sdg.dost.gov.ph/index.php/2024/09/01/11sustainablecitiesandcommunities/)
* [UN Pacific SDGs Goal 11](https://pacific.un.org/en/sdgs/11)
* [Local Government Academy (LGA) Publication](https://cdn.lga.gov.ph/publication/attachments/1590478478.pdf)

---

## 🎯 Project Objectives

1. **Inventory Management System:** Centralize stock tracking for LGU and barangay officials to record, monitor, update, and manage relief goods in real time.
2. **Disaster & Beneficiary Management System:** Track disaster incidents, affected families, individuals, and their specific assistance requirements.
3. **Donation Management System:** Automatically record incoming relief contributions and update available inventory dynamically.
4. **Distribution Management System:** Log the release of goods to beneficiaries and automatically deduct distributed items from inventory.

---

## MVC Backend

All Java source files are in the `LIB` package and the matching `LIB` folder. Classes outside that package, such as a future GUI, should import the classes they use (for example, `import LIB.Inventory;`) or use `import LIB.*;`.

The Java domain classes are the **Model** layer and own business rules such as transaction approval, role permission checks, and stock changes. `UserAccount` is an abstract base class; `AdminAccount`, `BarangayOfficialAccount`, and `EncoderAccount` inherit from it and override permission methods, demonstrating abstraction, inheritance, and runtime polymorphism. `BarangayScoped` is an interface implemented by accounts, inventory, disasters, evacuation centers, donations, and distributions so workspace membership can be checked consistently. The models also demonstrate encapsulation through private state and controlled methods, and composition through transactions containing item lines that reference inventory and batches. Accounts hold a barangay workspace where applicable, an email, active/inactive status, and a salted PBKDF2 password hash. `LoginController` can authenticate against an in-memory account list; SQL-backed account lookup and persistence are still pending.

Feature controllers coordinate calls to the models, while the GUI/View can call the controller methods when it is added. Each `Barangay` is a workspace for its inventory, disasters, evacuation centers, households, and staff. Active accounts of any role can modify disasters in workspaces they can access. `Beneficiaries` represents a household with at least one confirmed `FamilyMember` at registration; household size and vulnerability counts derive from that roster, and a designated member represents the household head when aid is received. A homeless household uses the barangay name as its address. Each member's age and senior/infant/PWD classifications are stored independently and entered based on human verification; the system does not infer classifications from age. Donations and distributions move through `DRAFT`, `PENDING`, and then `APPROVED` or `REJECTED`; only approval changes stock. Donation lines create distinct `InventoryBatch` records with received and optional expiry dates. Opening inventory is represented as an opening batch. Distribution lines can specify the batch to release; if only one batch has stock, it can be inferred, but the model requires an explicit batch when several are available rather than assuming an expiry/FIFO policy. Transaction and account data remain in memory until database persistence is added.

---

## 📦 Expected Output

The primary output is a web-based **Disaster Relief Goods Management System** featuring:
* **Accessible & Intuitive UI:** Tailored for LGU and Barangay Officials, incorporating accessibility features for Persons with Disabilities (PWD) personnel.
* **Core OOP Inventory Computation:** Deterministic algorithms leveraging Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts for exact inventory tracking.
* **AI-Assisted Reasoning Module:** An integrated AI model that analyzes community urgency levels, prioritizes essential goods, and assists in optimized dispatch decisions.

---

## 💡 Significance of the Study

This study advances software engineering and management research by demonstrating how **Artificial Intelligence can be layered onto classic Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) architectures**. Rather than completely replacing existing operational frameworks, this hybrid model tests how AI can enhance decision-making, priority sorting, and resource allocation without adding prohibitive costs or operational complexity.

---

## 👥 Target Beneficiaries

| Stakeholder Group | Expected Value & Outcome |
| :--- | :--- |
| **LGU & Barangay Staff** | Eliminates manual logbooks, reduces paperwork errors, and speeds up dispatch workflows. |
| **Barangay Residents** | Receives urgent, life-saving supplies faster and tailored to immediate community needs. |
| **Donors & NGOs** | Gains full transparency into inventory levels, ensuring aid reaches intended communities without waste. |
| **UN Organizations & DILG** | Obtains reliable data logging supporting SDG 11 urban risk reduction frameworks. |
| **PWD Personnel** | Interacts with an inclusive, accessible system interface designed for diverse operational roles. |
| **Future Researchers** | Serves as a baseline study for combining traditional software architectures with

### Phase 1: Requirement Analysis and Architecture Planning

| Task Description | Status |
| :--- | :--- |
| Establish the operational foundation for the Disaster Relief Goods Inventory and Distribution Management System. | |
| Finalize technical requirements, roles, and operational workflows. | |

### Phase 2: UI/UX Prototyping and Access Control

| Task Description | Status |
| :--- | :--- |
| Transition the 28 planned design screens into the interactive web application interface for BarangayCare. | |
| Construct the system around 10 major pages, establishing a central Dashboard branching out to Inventory, Disasters, Beneficiaries, Donations, Distribution, Reports, Audit Logs, and User Administration. | |
| Implement strict, hierarchical role permissions across the application. | |
| Grant Admin accounts comprehensive control over the workspace and user roles. | |
| Grant Barangay Officials the authority to manage records, confirm relief releases, and export data reports. | |
| Restrict Encoders strictly to data entry and drafting preparation. | |

### Phase 3: Core Application and Database Development

| Task Description | Status |
| :--- | :--- |
| Build the functional backend and interactive frontend relying on traditional Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts. | |
| Design the relational database architecture in MySQL to link disaster events, household records, and donor transactions, ensuring distributed quantities automatically deduct from available inventory. | |
| Develop a responsive React web application frontend utilizing persistent state management and real-time search filtering. | |
| Write the backend logic in Java using structured generic data models to handle incoming relief computations and track multi-variable metrics (e.g., senior citizens, infants, PWDs). | |

### Phase 4: AI Integration, Auditing, and Final Testing

| Task Description | Status |
| :--- | :--- |
| Integrate an AI model to evaluate real-time data and dynamically route goods based on urgency. | |
| Finalize the Audit Logs module to generate a read-only transaction history of all system activities and stock movements for strict accountability. | |
| Conduct comprehensive usability testing to guarantee platform reliability, efficiency, and full accessibility for PWD personnel. | |
| Prepare the completed system for final evaluation and noting by the faculty in-charge. | |

# Manage agent sessions in VS Code

* * *

A [session](/docs/agents/concepts/sessions) is the unit of work with an agent in Visual Studio Code. It brings together the workspace, code changes, and one or more chats for a task. Each chat has its own conversation history and context. This article describes how to manage these conversations and organize sessions across the [Chat view](/docs/agents/run/chat-view) and the [Agents window](/docs/agents/run/agents-window).

## Start an agent session

Start a new session when you begin an independent task or need a different workspace or configuration. For a fresh conversation that shares an existing session's workspace and code changes, [start another chat in that session](about:blank#_run-multiple-chats-in-a-session), where supported.

Choose the surface that matches your workflow:

*   Use the [Chat view](/docs/agents/run/chat-view#_start-a-session) for a workspace-scoped, code-first session beside the editor.
*   Use the [Agents window](/docs/agents/run/agents-window#_start-an-agent-session) to start and monitor sessions across workspaces, attach related projects or GitHub items, or start from an existing pull request. On Windows, you can also launch the Agents window directly by right-clicking the VS Code application icon in the taskbar and selecting **Agents Window**.

You can switch between these surfaces after you start a session. To compare all agent interfaces, see [Ways to work with agents](/docs/agents/overview#_ways-to-work-with-agents). To send and steer requests after a session starts, see [Use chat in VS Code](/docs/chat/chat-overview).

 Note

**For Local harness sessions:** Continue the session in the Chat view in an editor window. These sessions aren't available in the Agents window. Sessions from the OpenAI Codex extension are also editor-only. To use Codex in both interfaces, configure the [experimental Codex integration](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses#_codex).

## Move a chat to another folder or worktree

In the Agents window, move the current chat to another folder or a new Git worktree to continue a task without starting over. The move preserves its conversation history. This capability requires an Agent Host session that contains one chat and one local folder. Use the Copilot harness, or [Codex on the Agent Host (Experimental)](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses#_codex) in Interactive mode.

Ask the agent to move the chat with a natural-language prompt. This is an agent-tool request, not a separate move button. To move the current chat to an existing local folder on the same host:

```
Move this chat to <absolute folder path> and continue the current task there.
```

To isolate implementation in a new Git worktree, use this prompt from a folder session before implementation begins:

```
Continue this task in a new Git worktree of the current repository before implementing it.
```

When prompted, confirm the destination and whether to use the folder directly or create a worktree. Review any tool approval or Workspace Trust request. The agent finishes the current turn and then moves the chat. Wait for the workspace-change notice and for the chat to continue automatically before you send more prompts.

A folder move uses the files already in the destination and doesn't move or copy your existing files. A new worktree starts from committed Git state. Your uncommitted changes stay in the original folder, except for files copied by configured worktree include rules. Creating a worktree requires a Git repository with at least one commit. For complete prerequisites, file-copy behavior, and security considerations, see [Choose code isolation](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses#_choose-code-isolation).

## Manage session context

The context window control in the chat input shows how much of the model's context window the active chat is using. Hover over the control to see the token count, a usage breakdown by category, and the total AI credits consumed by the session.

![Screenshot of VS Code Chat view, showing the context window usage control in the chat input box.](/assets/docs/chat/copilot-chat/chat-context-window-control.png)

As the conversation grows, the control updates to reflect increasing context usage. The available context depends on the selected model.

How context changes across turns also affects prompt caching. Stable context lets the model provider reuse tokens from earlier requests, which lowers cost and latency. Use the [Cache Explorer](/docs/agents/agent-troubleshooting/cache-explorer) to check your cache hit rate.

Context compaction summarizes earlier conversation history to free space in the context window. Compaction lets you continue the same chat with less irrelevant history and reduces the tokens sent with subsequent requests.

# Use the Chat view

* * *

The Chat view is a code-first interface for asking questions and working with agents in the main Visual Studio Code window. Use it when your task centers on the current project and you want the editor, debugger, tests, extensions, and notebooks available alongside the conversation.

In this article, you learn how to open the Chat view, choose a layout, understand its interface, and start a workspace-scoped session. To compare it with other interfaces, see [Ways to work with agents](/docs/agents/overview#_ways-to-work-with-agents). For conversation mechanics shared with the [Agents window](/docs/agents/run/agents-window), see [Use chat in VS Code](/docs/chat/chat-overview).

## Prerequisites

## Open the Chat view

The Chat view opens in the Secondary Side Bar, next to your editor. To open the Chat view, use one of the following methods:

*   Select the **Chat** menu in the VS Code title bar, and then select **Open Chat**.

*   Use the keyboard shortcut ⌃⌘I (Windows, Linux Ctrl+Alt+I).

*   Run `code chat` from the command line to start chat from outside VS Code. Learn more about [starting chat from the command line](/docs/configure/command-line#_start-chat-from-the-command-line).

### Layout options

The Chat view offers several layout options within the main VS Code window. Choose the layout that best fits your workflow:

*   **Side bar** (default): select **New Chat (+)** > **New Chat**, or run the **Chat: New Chat** command. Best for keeping chat visible alongside your code.

*   **Editor tab**: select **New Chat (+)** > **New Chat Editor**, or run the **Chat: New Chat Editor** command. Best for giving chat more space or comparing sessions side by side.

*   **Separate window**: select **New Chat (+)** > **New Chat Window**, or run the **Chat: New Chat Window** command. Best for multi-monitor setups.

## Interface overview

The Chat view keeps the agent next to your code, so you can prompt, review, and edit in the same window. The Chat view has the following main areas:

1.  **Sessions list**: at the top of the view, where you can view and manage your sessions for the current workspace. Learn more about the [sessions list](/docs/agents/run/sessions/manage-sessions#_sessions-list).

2.  **Chat conversation**: in the center, where you see the conversation history and the agent's responses, including the changes it makes to your code.

3.  **Chat input**: at the bottom, where you type prompts and configure the session with the **Session Target**, **Agent**, **Language model**, and **Permissions** controls.

![Screenshot showing the Chat view with the sessions list, conversation, and chat input.](/assets/docs/agents/agents-overview/chat-view-expanded.png)

 Tip

To inspect a chat response with a keyboard or screen reader, run **Open Accessible View** (⌥F2 (Windows Alt+F2, Linux Shift+Alt+F2)). Learn more about the [Accessible View](/docs/configure/accessibility/accessibility#_accessible-view).

The Chat view operates in two modes: compact and side-by-side. Use the toggle control in the top-right corner of the Chat view to switch between them. In compact mode, the sessions list and conversation share the same panel. In side-by-side mode, the sessions list stays visible next to the conversation. Learn more about [sessions list layout options](/docs/agents/run/sessions/manage-sessions#_sessions-list).

### Switch chats within a session

With a harness that supports multiple chats, such as Copilot or Claude, a session can contain a main chat and additional peer chats. In the **Sessions** view, expand the main chat row and select a peer to open its conversation in the Chat view.

You can continue peer chats created in the Agents window without starting a new session. For creation steps, navigation options, and interface-specific controls, see [Run multiple chats in a session](/docs/agents/run/sessions/manage-sessions#_run-multiple-chats-in-a-session).

## Start a session

To start a workspace-scoped session, select **New Chat** (`+`) or press ⌘N (Windows, Linux Ctrl+N). Before you send the first prompt, use the chat input controls to choose a **Session Target**, **Agent**, **Language model**, and **Permissions**. For a first coding task, use **Copilot**, **Agent**, **Auto**, and **Manual permissions**, as shown in the [agents quickstart](/docs/agents/quickstart). Available choices depend on your account, installed providers, and organization policies. Learn how to [identify your current harness](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses#_identify-your-current-harness) or [compare agent harnesses](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses#_compare-agent-harnesses).

Type a prompt and press Enter. For shared request, context, and conversation controls, see [Use chat in VS Code](/docs/chat/chat-overview). For session context, history, and organization, see [Manage agent sessions](/docs/agents/run/sessions/manage-sessions).

## Work with the agent

Because the Chat view runs in the main VS Code window, you can inspect agent edits in the editor, follow terminal activity, debug the application, and run tasks or tests without switching surfaces. The agent also has access to supported extensions and can [work with Jupyter notebooks](/docs/agents/guides/notebooks-with-ai). When you connect to a [remote workspace](/docs/remote/remote-overview), the session uses the same remote project context and tools.

The Copilot harness applies and saves edits directly to the selected folder or worktree. Select a changed file in the response to inspect its diff, or set chat.checkpoints.showFileChanges to show a changed-files summary after each request. For revisions, checkpoints, harness-specific review workflows, and integrating changes, see [Review AI-generated code edits](/docs/agents/run/review-code-edits).
